endorsements.name: Kevin Finisterre
endorsements.label: CVE-2022-2675
endorsements.description: Using off-the-shelf commodity hardware, the Unitree Go 1 robotics platform version H0.1.7 and H0.1.9 (using firmware version 0.1.35) can be powered down by an attacker within normal RF range without authentication. Other versions may be affected, such as the A1.

endorsements.name: Kevin Finisterre
endorsements.label: CVE-2025-2894
endorsements.description: The Go1 also known as "The World's First Intelligence Bionic Quadruped Robot Companion of Consumer Level," contains an undocumented backdoor that can enable the manufacturer, and anyone in possession of the correct API key, complete remote control over the affected robotic device using the CloudSail remote access service.
endorsements.subtitle: CVE · Severity: MEDIUM (CVSS 3.1, 6.6)

endorsements.name: Kevin Finisterre
endorsements.label: CVE-2025-35027
endorsements.description: Multiple robotic products by Unitree sharing a common firmware, including the Go2, G1, H1, and B2 devices, contain a command injection vulnerability. By setting a malicious string when configuring the on-board WiFi via a BLE module of an affected robot, then triggering a restart of the WiFi service, an attacker can ultimately trigger commands to be run as root via the wpa_supplicant_restart.sh shell script. All Unitree models use firmware derived from the same codebase (MIT Cheetah), and the two major forks are the G1 (humanoid) and Go2 (quadruped) branches.
endorsements.subtitle: CVE · Severity: HIGH (CVSS 3.1, 7.3)
